name: acquired perforating dermatosis
aliases: perforating dermatosis of chronic renal failure and diabetes

clinicalPearls: Umbrella term for perforating disorders arising in adults, classically associated with chronic kidney disease and diabetes mellitus, characterised by transepidermal elimination of dermal material.
Presents as intensely pruritic, umbilicated papules and nodules with a central keratotic plug, favouring the extensor surfaces of the limbs and the trunk.
Koebnerisation is prominent; scratching provokes new lesions arranged in linear streaks, and the itch-scratch cycle perpetuates the eruption.
Histology shows a channel of transepidermal elimination extruding degenerate collagen, elastic fibres or keratin through the epidermis or a follicular infundibulum.

The four classic perforating dermatoses (Kyrle disease, reactive perforating collagenosis, perforating folliculitis, elastosis perforans serpiginosa) show overlapping features when acquired in adults, hence the unifying term.
Strongly linked to end-stage renal disease on haemodialysis and to poorly controlled diabetic nephropathy; screening for occult renal or metabolic disease is warranted at presentation.
Management targets the underlying disease and pruritus: emollients, topical retinoids or corticosteroids, phototherapy (narrowband ultraviolet B), and control of uraemia or glycaemia.
Reported associations extend beyond renal disease to hypothyroidism, hepatic dysfunction, malignancy and certain drugs (notably targeted anticancer agents).
reference.pathophysiology: Acquired perforating dermatosis reflects abnormal transepidermal elimination of altered dermal connective tissue, in which degenerate collagen and/or elastic fibres, and sometimes keratinous debris, are extruded through the epidermis or follicular epithelium. In the setting of chronic kidney disease and diabetes, microangiopathy, deposition of substances that cannot be cleared by failing kidneys, dermal microdeposits (including calcium and urate), and advanced glycation end-products are thought to injure dermal matrix and provoke a foreign-body-like elimination response. Repetitive trauma from scratching (driven by uraemic or metabolic pruritus) initiates and perpetuates lesions through Koebnerisation, and epidermal hyperproliferation forms the characteristic keratotic plug overlying a perforating channel.
additionalInvestigations: skin biopsy with elastic tissue and connective tissue stains to demonstrate the perforating channel and eliminated material
renal function tests (urea, creatinine, estimated glomerular filtration rate)
liver function tests and thyroid function tests
full blood count and calcium/phosphate profile
age-appropriate malignancy screening where clinically indicated
redFlags: new-onset perforating eruption without known renal or metabolic disease, prompting evaluation for occult systemic illness or malignancy
rapidly progressive lesions or systemic symptoms (weight loss, night sweats) suggesting underlying neoplasm
signs of secondary bacterial infection of excoriated lesions
intractable pruritus indicating poorly controlled uraemia or hyperglycaemia
reference.prognosis: The eruption tends to be chronic and relapsing, mirroring the course of the underlying renal or metabolic disease; lesions may improve with control of the systemic condition or after renal transplantation but often persist while pruritus and scratching continue.
pitfalls: attributing intensely pruritic umbilicated papules to simple prurigo and overlooking the diagnostic transepidermal elimination on biopsy
failing to investigate for underlying chronic kidney disease, diabetes or occult malignancy at first presentation
biopsying an excoriated or superinfected lesion rather than an intact keratotic papule, obscuring the histology
expecting durable clearance from topical therapy alone without addressing the systemic driver and the itch-scratch cycle
